## 1. New LLM Versions / Major AI Lab Tools

- **Date:** 2026-08-31  
  **Source:** [OpenAI — Previewing GPT-5.6 Sol](https://openai.com/index/previewing-gpt-5-6-sol/)  
  **Summary:** OpenAI previewed GPT-5.6 Sol, positioning it as a next-generation model with stronger coding, science, and cybersecurity capabilities, paired with an updated safety stack.  
  **Why it matters:** Signals OpenAI’s next closed frontier-model step, with explicit emphasis on high-value technical domains and safety controls.

- **Date:** 2026-08-31  
  **Source:** [OpenAI — GPT-5.6 in Kiro](https://openai.com/index/gpt-5-6-in-kiro/)  
  **Summary:** OpenAI said the GPT-5.6 family — including Sol, Terra, and Luna — is now available in Kiro for planning, building, reviewing, and testing software.  
  **Why it matters:** Moves GPT-5.6 into an applied software-agent workflow rather than limiting the announcement to model access.

- **Date:** 2026-08-31  
  **Source:** [OpenAI Help Center — Using Codex with your ChatGPT plan](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11369540-using-codex-with-your-chatgpt-plan)  
  **Summary:** OpenAI’s Codex guidance says GPT-5.4 and GPT-5.4 mini are no longer available through ChatGPT-plan Codex access as of August 31, 2026; users are directed to GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-5.6 Luna. API-key usage is not affected.  
  **Why it matters:** Confirms GPT-5.6 variants are replacing prior Codex defaults for ChatGPT-plan users, creating a near-term migration requirement.

## 2. FOSS / Open-Weight LMs & Tools

- **Date:** 2026-08-30  
  **Source:** [Hugging Face — zai-org/GLM-5.3](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3)  
  **Summary:** Z.ai released GLM-5.3, an open-weight model based on the GLM-5.2 base with post-training improvements focused on complex coding, long-horizon agent tasks, and cyber benchmark performance.  
  **Why it matters:** Adds another major open-weight option for coding and agentic workloads, with direct relevance to teams evaluating self-hosted or modifiable alternatives to closed coding agents.
